items.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: or actually was it Mario Bauza, is he the guy that—

ctx.x: He was a pioneer, yeah, he was. He was working with George Shearing — Cal was from here, from the West Coast, he’s from San Mateo, which is down the Peninsula. He and Merv Griffin went to prep school or high school together, so they were buddies. But anyway Cal, kind of a self-taught player, but worked with George Shearing for a while and while he was with George Shearing in New York, Al McKibbon was on the band and Al took him around the corner to the Palladium one night and he heard Tito Puente and Machito…

Latin jazz thing together, which is what he did. He had guys from here that could play both, because they had to play both ways. And then he said that they would barnstorm, where they would get in a car and go across the country and work all these places between here and New York where they had never heard anything like that, never heard Latin music. In fact he ran into some resistance in some places he said, they didn’t want to hear that. And so he was a pioneer. Of course I think Dizzy was the first guy — or…
He was with Dizzy, wasn’t he?
